target_customer: Quant funds, market makers, prop trading firms and researchers who need normalized prediction market data
problem: Prediction market data is fragmented across venues such as Kalshi and Polymarket. Oddpool offers a universal market identifier and tick-level history with order book depth for backtesting.
business_model: Usage-based API with self-serve tiers (free, $30 and $100 per month) and per-call institutional pricing
product_category: Financial data infrastructure for prediction markets

founders.name: Ritesh Malpani
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO while his bio says Founder, CTO. Roommates with the co-founder since freshman year.

founders.name: Avi Arora
founders.background_notes: YC bio says Founder, CEO. Role conflict between listing and bio.

exit.reason: Reports say Oddpool joined Kalshi to build institutional data tools after talks with Kalshi's CEO; terms not disclosed. Outlets differ on whether it was an acquisition or joining.

competitors.name: EntityML
competitors.what: YC-backed provider of live and historical L2 order book data for Kalshi and Polymarket
competitors.traction_then: Historical coverage for Kalshi from 2026-02-17 per its docs

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing and normalizing full order books across venues, mapping equivalent markets and serving tick history is solid data engineering; the founders claim 100K+ TPS experience.

defensibility.rationale: Historical order book archives compound over time, but several vendors and open-source tools (pmxt, CoinAPI) offered similar feeds.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Kalshi absorbed the team in September 2026 and also launched its own terminal-style interface in June 2026.

market_need_then: Prediction market volume and institutional interest rose sharply in 2025 and 2026, creating demand for clean historical data and backtesting.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short, declarative copy aimed at quants and coding agents

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by crypto and startup outlets mainly for the seed and Kalshi deal.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable name tied to odds and liquidity pools with a clear wordmark, but no press about the brand itself beyond deal coverage.

outcome_analysis: Oddpool was a two-person spring 2026 company serving a fast-growing prediction market niche. It reported a $3M seed in early September 2026 and joined Kalshi the same month, so it exited within months of the batch. The acquirer is also the largest venue it sold data about, which shows the platform risk of data vendors in a venue-dominated market.
notes: Seed amount reported by The SaaS News and Dealroom (both date it September 2026, no investors named); treat as two outlets with the same underlying report. Outlets name a co-founder Dhruv in one place and Avi Arora and Ritesh Malpani in another; this record follows the YC page. Deal described as joining Kalshi (CryptoRank, KuCoin, CoinGape, dated 2026-09-04) versus acquired with a Dealroom date of 2026-09-16. EntityML source date is approximate and based on its data-coverage start date; its page is undated.
